title: Shanti Mantra: May We Hear Good
meter: Meter: Vedic Trishtubh (about 11 syllables per line)
meterNote: This is a Vedic prayer in Trishtubh meter. Vedic verses were chanted with pitch accents and don't always fit the strict syllable counts of classical meters, so the scanner is not used here.
translation: O gods, may we hear what is good with our ears; O worshipful ones, may we see what is good with our eyes. With steady limbs and bodies, praising you, may we live out the life the gods have given. May Indra of great fame grant us well-being; may Pushan, who knows all, grant us well-being; may Tarkshya, whose wheel is never harmed, grant us well-being; may Brihaspati grant us well-being. Om, peace, peace, peace.
translation_hi: हे देवताओ, हम कानों से शुभ सुनें; हे पूजनीयो, हम आँखों से शुभ देखें। स्थिर अंगों और शरीर से आपकी स्तुति करते हुए हम देवताओं द्वारा दी गई आयु जिएँ। महान यशस्वी इंद्र हमारा कल्याण करें; सर्वज्ञ पूषा हमारा कल्याण करें; अरिष्टनेमि तार्क्ष्य हमारा कल्याण करें; बृहस्पति हमारा कल्याण करें। ॐ शांति, शांति, शांति।

words.note: As in bhadrayai in the Devi Stuti.
Vedic instrumental plural; classical Sanskrit says कर्णैः. Karna also means hypotenuse (Lilavati verse 12)!
su + asti, 'it is well'. Hence swastika.
The Vedic god of paths and nourishment.
Teacher of the gods (suraguru in Lingashtakam 8).

grammar: Vedic Sanskrit: forms like कर्णेभिः, अक्षभिः are older than classical Sanskrit (कर्णैः, अक्षिभिः). This prayer comes from the Atharvaveda, to which the Mandukya belongs.
Optative 'may we': शृणुयाम, पश्येम, व्यशेम, the mood of wishes, like पठेत् in the Lingashtakam.
Three times shanti: traditionally for peace from the three kinds of suffering: from oneself, from other beings, and from nature. These are the trayah-shula of Rudrashtakam verse 5.
Svasti + dative: स्वस्ति नः 'well-being to us', like नमः + dative.
